instruction: Can maize intercropping help with FAW?
response: Crop diversification can reduce FAW pressure in some systems. A 2025 Nigeria study reported lower FAW incidence and damage in maize intercropped with soybean than in sole maize. Treat this as location-specific evidence, not a guarantee for every farm. Source: Jibril & Ahmed (2025), AGRIS.

instruction: Ìfihàn àwòrán: 55% ọ̀gbìn ológun, 40% ìdin míì. Àgbẹ̀: Ìdin náà jẹ́ brown. Ṣé FAW ni?
response: Má ṣe pinnu lórí àwọ̀ nikan. Ṣé orí ìdin náà ní àmì Y tí ó yí padà? Ṣé àmì mẹ́rin dúdú wà lórí apá ara tó sún mọ́ ìkẹyìn? Source: CABI Fall Armyworm Field Handbook.

instruction: Ìfihàn àwòrán: 58% ọ̀gbìn ológun, 39% cutworm. Àgbẹ̀: Wọ́n ń gé àwọn seedling mi. Ṣé FAW ni?
response: Má ṣe dá a lórí ìgbà kan. Ṣé wọ́n ń gé ewéko náà nítòsí ilẹ̀, tàbí ṣé o ń rí ìbàjẹ́ tuntun àti frass nínú ihò? Source: FAO/CABI FAW identification guidance.

instruction: Ìfihàn àwòrán: 60% ọ̀gbìn ológun, 35% kò dájú. Àgbẹ̀: Mo rí egg mass lórí ewé. Ṣé FAW ni?
response: Mi ò lè dájú pátápátá láti inú èyí nikan. Ṣé egg mass náà ní irun tàbí scales lórí rẹ̀, àti níbo ni ó wà lórí ewéko náà? Source: CABI Fall Armyworm Field Handbook.

instruction: Farmer: Ahụrụ m egg mass n'akwụkwọ.\nAssistant: Lelee ya nke ọma.\nFarmer: Kedu ihe m ga-achọ?
response: Lelee ma eggs ahụ bụ otu mass ma nwee ntutu ma ọ bụ scales n'elu; leleekwa olulu ọka maka mmebi ọhụrụ. Ọ bụrụ na ị maghị, ajụla ịkọ na ọ bụ FAW. Source: CABI Fall Armyworm Field Handbook.

instruction: What if the infestation comes back after I removed larvae?
response: Restart systematic scouting and look for fresh damage, frass, eggs and surviving larvae. Repeated outbreaks are a reason to improve field monitoring and integrated prevention rather than relying on one action. Source: FAO, Integrated Management of FAW on Maize (2018).

instruction: Intercropping nwere ike nyere aka megide fall armyworm?
response: Crop diversification nwere ike ibelata nrụgide FAW n'ụfọdụ usoro ugbo. Nnyocha Naịjirịa 2025 hụrụ obere FAW incidence na damage mgbe a kụrụ soybean na ọka ọnụ ma e jiri ya tụnyere sole maize. Nke a abụghị nkwa maka ubi niile. Source: Jibril & Ahmed (2025), AGRIS.

instruction: Alamar hoton gona: 51% kwaron soja, 46% stem borer. Manomi: Masara tana lalacewa a ciki. Me zan yi?
response: Ina bukatar ƙarin alama kafin in gane kwaron. Sabuwar barna tana cikin ramin masara ne tare da bayan gari mai laima, ko kuma akwai ramuka a jikin sanda tare da ƙurar busasshe? Source: FAO/CABI FAW identification guidance.

instruction: How often I suppose check my maize for fall armyworm?
response: For smallholder fields, FAO says enter the field at least once every week, and check more often when things dey change quickly. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Kí ni mo lè ṣe tí mo bá rí àkójọpọ̀ ẹyin tàbí àwọn ìdin kékeré?
response: Tí ó bá ṣeé ṣe, yọ kí o sì pa àkójọpọ̀ ẹyin àti ìdin kékeré run níbi tí o bá rí wọn. Èyí jẹ́ ọ̀kan lára àwọn ìlànà kékeré tó wà nínú iṣakoso àpapọ̀ FAO. Source: FAO, Integrated Management of FAW on Maize (2018).

instruction: Farmer: E wepụrụ m larvae site n'aka.\nAssistant: Gaa n'ihu na scouting.\nFarmer: Ha lọghachiri otu izu gachara. Gịnị ka m ga-eme?
response: Malite scouting opekata mpe otu ugboro kwa izu ma ọ bụ karịa mgbe mgbanwe dị ukwuu. Chọọ eggs, mmebi ọhụrụ na frass, ma lelee natural enemies. Source: FAO, Integrated Management of FAW on Maize (2018).

instruction: Vision signal: 55% fall armyworm, 40% another caterpillar. Farmer: The caterpillar is brown. Should I treat it as FAW?
response: Do not guess from colour alone. Can you describe the head marking and the spots on the last body segments, and tell me whether fresh frass is present in the maize whorl? Source: CABI Fall Armyworm Field Handbook.

instruction: Me zan yi idan na sami ƙwai ko ƙananan tsutsotsi?
response: Inda ya yiwu, ɗauki tarin ƙwai ko ƙananan tsutsotsi ka lalata su. Wannan mataki ne mai sauƙi da FAO ta haɗa cikin tsarin haɗa hanyoyin sarrafa kwaron soja. Source: FAO, Integrated Management of FAW on Maize (2018).

instruction: Ṣé fífọ̀nà gbin àgbàdo pẹ́ lè mú ọ̀gbìn ológun pọ̀ sí i?
response: Gbígbin pẹ́ lè fi àgbàdo kékeré tí ó rọrùn sí ewu ọ̀gbìn ológun. FAO dámọ̀ràn yíyẹra fún gbígbin pẹ́ gẹ́gẹ́ bí apá ìṣàkóso àpapọ̀. Source: FAO, Five things to know about Fall Armyworm.

instruction: Ta yaya zan gane cewa maƙiyan halitta suna kashe kwaron soja?
response: FAO ta ambaci ƙwai masu duhu ko marasa daidaito, farin kokon parasitoid a kan tsutsa, da gawar tsutsa mai tauri ko laushi a matsayin alamun maƙiyan halitta ko ƙwayoyin cuta. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Mmebi dị ugbu a apụwo mana oghere ochie ka dị. Gịnị ka m ga-eme?
response: Ejila oghere ochie naanị mee mkpebi. Lelee olulu ọzọ maka mmebi ọhụrụ ma ọ bụ frass ọhụrụ, gụọ naanị osisi ndị nwere infestation ugbu a. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Vision signal: 51% fall armyworm, 46% stem borer. Farmer: Ọka m na-emebi n'ime. Kedu ihe m ga-eme?
response: Achọrọ m otu ihe ọzọ tupu m mata ya. Mmebi ọhụrụ dị n'olulu na frass mmiri, ka ọ bụ e nwere oghere n'osisi na dry sawdust-like material? Source: FAO/CABI FAW identification guidance.

instruction: Farmer: The holes from last week still dey.\nAssistant: Count fresh damage only.\nFarmer: So I count the plant today?
response: Only count it as currently infested when you see fresh damage or fresh frass showing current activity. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Àgbẹ̀: Ṣé mo lè lo insecticide míì torí ọ̀gbìn ológun padà?\nOlùrànlọ́wọ́: Ọ̀rọ̀ kemika gbọ́dọ̀ tẹ̀lé àkọọlẹ̀ ọja tó forúkọ sílẹ̀.\nÀgbẹ̀: Kí ni mo yẹ kí n ṣàyẹ̀wò?
response: Jẹ́risi pé ọja náà forúkọ sílẹ̀ fún irúgbìn àti kokoro yẹn ní agbègbè rẹ, kí o sì tẹ̀lé àkọọlẹ̀ rẹ fún lílo, ààbò àti àkókò ìdúró kí o tó kórè. Má ṣe gba iye lílo ọja míì kí o yí i padà sí ọja yìí. Source: FAO position on pesticide use for FAW.

instruction: Enwere m fall armyworm n'ubi. Gịnị bụ ihe mbụ m kwesịrị ime?
response: Kwenye na mmebi ọhụrụ na frass ọhụrụ kwekọrọ na FAW, dekọọ ebe ọ dị, ma gaa n'ihu na scouting. Jikọta monitoring, manual control na ichekwa natural enemies. Source: FAO, Integrated Management of FAW on Maize (2018).

instruction: Natural enemies na-enyere aka megide fall armyworm?
response: Ee. Ants, earwigs, predatory bugs, birds, parasitoid wasps na pathogens nwere ike igbu fall armyworm. Mụta ịmata ha ma chekwaa ha. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: How do I sample a maize field for FAW?
response: Walk the field in a W pattern. At the start, each turn and the end, inspect 10 plants in a row for recent whorl damage or fresh frass, then record the number currently infested. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Fall armyworm nwere ike ibi na crop ndị ọzọ?
response: Ee. FAW nwere ike iri ọtụtụ ụdị osisi, ọ bụ ezie na maize bụ otu n'ime preferred hosts ya. Ya mere lelee usoro crop gị dum. Source: FAO FAW Monitoring/Identification guidance.

instruction: Báwo ni mo ṣe lè gba àpẹẹrẹ nínú oko mi fún ọ̀gbìn ológun?
response: Rìn ní ìrísí lẹ́tà W. Ní ìbẹ̀rẹ̀, ní gbogbo ìyípadà, àti ní ìkẹyìn, ṣàyẹ̀wò ewéko mẹ́wàá ní àlàfo fún ìbàjẹ́ tuntun tàbí frass tuntun nínú ihò, kí o sì kọ iye ewéko tó ní ìjàkadi lọ́wọ́. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Na sami kwaron soja a gona. Menene mataki na farko?
response: Da farko ka tabbatar da alamun sabuwar barna da sabon bayan gari sun dace da kwaron soja, ka rubuta inda matsalar take, sannan ka ci gaba da bincike. Yi amfani da hanyoyi da dama tare, ciki har da sa ido da kare maƙiyan halitta. Source: FAO, Integrated Management of FAW on Maize (2018).

instruction: Ìfihàn àwòrán: 51% ọ̀gbìn ológun, 46% stem borer. Àgbẹ̀: Àgbàdo mi ń bàjẹ́ nínú. Kí ni mo ṣe?
response: Mo nílò àmì kan síi kí n tó dájú. Ṣé ìbàjẹ́ tuntun wà nínú ihò pẹ̀lú frass tí ó tutu, tàbí ṣé ihò àti ẹgẹ́ igi gbígbẹ wà lórí igi? Source: FAO/CABI FAW identification guidance.

instruction: Will maize always lose most of its yield when FAW damages leaves?
response: Not necessarily. FAO notes that maize can compensate for some FAW leaf damage, so the farmer should scout and assess current infestation rather than assuming every damaged plant will have severe yield loss. Source: FAO, FAW management guidance (2018).

instruction: How often should I scout maize for fall armyworm?
response: For a smallholder field, enter the field at least once a week and more often when conditions are changing. Scout systematically rather than checking only the field edge. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Ṣé kí n dá àgbàdo pọ̀ mọ́ irúgbìn mìíràn lè rànwọ́?
response: Ìdapọ̀ irúgbìn lè dín ìjàkadi FAW kù ní àwọn eto kan. Ìwádìí Nàìjíríà 2025 rí ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ àti ìbàjẹ́ FAW kéré síi ní àgbàdo tí wọ́n darapọ̀ mọ́ soybean ju àgbàdo nikan lọ. Èyí kì í ṣe ìdánilójú fún gbogbo oko. Source: Jibril & Ahmed (2025), AGRIS.

instruction: Ugboro ole ka m kwesịrị ịlele ubi ọka m maka fall armyworm?
response: Maka obere ugbo, FAO na-atụ aro ka ị banye n'ubi opekata mpe otu ugboro kwa izu, ma mee nyocha ugboro ugboro mgbe ọnọdụ na-agbanwe. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Menene bayan gari (frass), kuma me ya sa yake da muhimmanci?
response: Bayan gari shi ne tarkacen da tsutsa ke fitarwa, mai kama da ƙurar itace, da ake samu a ramin masara. Sabon bayan gari tare da sabuwar barna na nuna cewa tsutsa tana cin ganyen a yanzu. Source: FAO Guidance Note 2 (2018); CABI Field Handbook.

instruction: Ṣé rírí moth agbalagba túmọ̀ sí pé gbogbo oko ti ní ìjàkadi?
response: Rárá. Moth ń fi hàn pé FAW wà ní agbègbè, ṣùgbọ́n kò fi hàn pé gbogbo ewéko ní ìdin alààyè. Ṣàyẹ̀wò ihò àgbàdo fún ìbàjẹ́ tuntun àti frass. Source: FAO FAMEWS/FAW monitoring guidance.

instruction: Vision signal: 60% fall armyworm, 35% uncertain. Farmer: Ahụrụ m egg mass n'akwụkwọ. Ọ bụ FAW?
response: Enweghị m ike ikwenye site na nke a naanị. Egg mass ahụ nwere ntutu ma ọ bụ scales? Ọ dị n'ebe dị aṅaa n'osisi? Source: CABI Fall Armyworm Field Handbook.

instruction: How I fit scout my maize field for FAW?
response: Walk the field in a W pattern. At the start, every turn and the end, inspect 10 plants in a row for fresh whorl damage or fresh frass, then record the plants currently infested. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Àgbẹ̀: Mo yọ àwọn ìdin náà pẹ̀lú ọwọ́.\nOlùrànlọ́wọ́: Máa tẹ̀síwájú pẹ̀lú ìwòran.\nÀgbẹ̀: Wọ́n padà lẹ́yìn ọ̀sẹ̀ kan. Kí ni mo ṣe?
response: Padà sí ìwòran o kere tán lẹ́ẹ̀kan lọ́sẹ̀, tàbí ju bẹ́ẹ̀ lọ nígbà tí ìṣòro ń yí padà. Wá ẹyin, ìbàjẹ́ tuntun àti frass, kí o sì ṣàyẹ̀wò àwọn ọ̀tá àdánidá. Source: FAO, Integrated Management of FAW on Maize (2018).

instruction: Wetin I suppose record when I dey scout FAW?
response: Record the plot, your sampling route, number of plants currently infested, crop condition and natural enemies you see. Consistent records help you compare changes over time. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Me zan rubuta lokacin da nake duba gonar kwaron soja?
response: Rubuta gonar ko filin, hanyar bincike, adadin shuke-shuken da ke fama a yanzu, yanayin amfanin gona da abin da ka lura da shi game da maƙiyan halitta. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Old damage for maize don mean say fall armyworm still dey there?
response: No. Old holes alone no prove current infestation. Check for fresh leaf damage or fresh frass inside the whorl before you count the plant as currently infested. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Shin jinkirin shuka masara na iya ƙara matsalar kwaron soja?
response: Jinkirin shuka na iya sa ƙananan masara su kasance cikin matsin kwaro. FAO ta haɗa guje wa jinkirin shuka cikin hanyoyin haɗaɗɗen sarrafa kwaron soja. Source: FAO, Five things to know about Fall Armyworm.

instruction: Ọ̀ bụ mmebi akwụkwọ naanị zuru ezu iji kwuo na ọ bụ fall armyworm?
response: Mba. Oghere ọhụrụ na frass n'ime olulu bụ ihe ngosi siri ike, mana nyochaa caterpillar maka akara pụrụ iche tupu ị kwado diagnosis. Source: FAO Guidance Note 2 (2018); CABI Field Handbook.

instruction: Shin ganin malam buɗe ido na kwaron soja ya isa in ce gonata ta kamu?
response: A'a. Ganin babban kwaro yana nuna cewa FAW na kusa, amma ba ya tabbatar da tsutsa mai rai a kowace shuka. Ka duba ramin masara don sabuwar barna ko bayan gari. Source: FAO FAMEWS/FAW monitoring guidance.

instruction: Late planting fit make fall armyworm problem worse?
response: It can expose young maize to FAW pressure. FAO includes avoiding late planting as part of integrated management. Source: FAO, Five things to know about Fall Armyworm.

instruction: Me zan yi idan kwaron soja ya dawo bayan na cire tsutsotsi?
response: Ka koma ga bincike na tsari, ka nemi sabon cizo, bayan gari, ƙwai da tsutsotsi, sannan ka duba ko ana kare maƙiyan halitta da sauran matakan haɗaɗɗen sarrafawa. Source: FAO, Integrated Management of FAW on Maize (2018).

instruction: Báwo ni mo ṣe mọ̀ pé àwọn ọ̀tá àdánidá ń kọlu ọ̀gbìn ológun?
response: FAO mẹ́nuba ẹyin tí ó ṣokunkun tàbí tí kò dọ́gba, funfun parasitoid cocoons, àti àwọn ìdin tó ti kú gẹ́gẹ́ bí àmì iṣẹ́ ọ̀tá àdánidá tàbí pathogens. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Kí ni frass, kí ló sì ṣe pàtàkì fún ìdámọ̀ ọ̀gbìn ológun?
response: Frass ni ìdọ̀tí ìdin tó dàbí ẹ̀gẹ́ igi tí a lè rí nínú ihò àgbàdo. Frass tuntun pẹ̀lú ìbàjẹ́ tuntun fi hàn pé ìdin ń jẹ ẹ́ lọ́wọ́. Source: FAO Guidance Note 2 (2018); CABI Field Handbook.

instruction: Ịkụ ọka n'oge nwere ike imetụta fall armyworm?
response: Ịkụ oge adịghị mma ma ọ bụ oge gachara nwere ike ime ka osisi ọka dị obere nọgide na-edo onwe ha n'okpuru nrụgide pest. FAO na-atụ aro izere late planting n'ime integrated management. Source: FAO, Five things to know about Fall Armyworm.

instruction: Manomi: Na cire tsutsotsin kwaron soja da hannu.\nMataimaki: Ka ci gaba da dubawa.\nManomi: Sun dawo bayan mako guda. Me zan yi?
response: Ka koma yin bincike aƙalla sau ɗaya a mako, ko fiye idan matsalar tana canzawa. Duba ƙwai, sabuwar barna da sabon bayan gari, kuma ka lura da maƙiyan halitta. Source: FAO, Integrated Management of FAW on Maize (2018).

instruction: Vision signal: 58% fall armyworm, 39% cutworm. Farmer: Something dey cut my seedlings. Na FAW?
response: No assume. The seedlings dey cut near the soil line, or you also see fresh holes and frass inside the whorl? Source: FAO/CABI FAW identification guidance.

instruction: Vision signal: 51% fall armyworm, 46% stem borer. Farmer: My maize is damaged inside. What should I do?
response: I need one more clue before identifying it. Is the fresh damage mainly in the whorl, with moist frass, or are there holes and dry sawdust-like material along the stalk? Source: FAO Guidance Note 2 (2018); CABI Field Handbook.

instruction: Gịnị bụ frass, gịnị mere o ji baa uru n'ịchọpụta fall armyworm?
response: Frass bụ ihe mkpofu caterpillar dị ka ntụ osisi nke a na-ahụ n'ime olulu ọka. Frass ọhụrụ tinyere mmebi ọhụrụ na-egosi na larva ka na-eri nri. Source: FAO Guidance Note 2 (2018); CABI Field Handbook.

instruction: Àgbẹ̀: Mo rí àkójọpọ̀ ẹyin lórí ewé.\nOlùrànlọ́wọ́: Ṣàyẹ̀wò rẹ dáadáa.\nÀgbẹ̀: Kí ni mo yẹ kí n wá?
response: Wá bóyá ẹyin náà wà nínú àkójọpọ̀ kan tí ó ní irun tàbí scales lórí rẹ̀; tún wo ihò àgbàdo fún ìbàjẹ́ tuntun. Tí o kò bá dájú, má ṣe ṣe àfojúsùn pé FAW ni. Source: CABI Fall Armyworm Field Handbook.

instruction: Vision signal: 60% fall armyworm, 35% uncertain. Farmer: I found an egg mass on a maize leaf. Is it FAW?
response: Not from that information alone. Does the egg mass have a covering of hairs or scales, and where on the plant is it located? A photo or a description of its size and appearance would help. Source: CABI Fall Armyworm Field Handbook.

instruction: Shin kwaron soja yana rayuwa a wasu amfanin gona?
response: Eh. FAW na iya cin nau'ikan tsirrai da yawa, ko da yake masara na daga cikin shuke-shuken da ya fi so. Wannan ya sa ya dace a duba tsarin gonar gaba ɗaya. Source: FAO FAW Monitoring/Identification guidance.

instruction: Ịhụ moth okenye pụtara na ubi m nwere infestation?
response: Mba. Moth na-egosi na FAW dị n'akụkụ, ma ọ naghị egosi na osisi ọ bụla nwere live larva. Lelee olulu ọka maka mmebi ọhụrụ na frass. Source: FAO FAMEWS/FAW monitoring guidance.

instruction: Farmer: I remove the larvae by hand.\nAssistant: Keep scouting.\nFarmer: They come back after one week. Wetin I do?
response: Go back to systematic scouting at least weekly, or more often when the situation changes. Look for eggs, fresh damage and fresh frass, and watch the natural enemies too. Source: FAO, Integrated Management of FAW on Maize (2018).

instruction: Gịnị ka m ga-eme ma fall armyworm lọta mgbe m wepụsịrị larvae?
response: Malite scouting ọzọ n'usoro, chọọ mmebi ọhụrụ, frass, eggs na larvae, ma lelee ma a na-echekwa natural enemies na integrated practices ndị ọzọ. Source: FAO, Integrated Management of FAW on Maize (2018).

instruction: What signs show that natural enemies are attacking FAW?
response: FAO notes uneven or darkened egg masses, white silken parasitoid cocoons, and hard or soft larval cadavers as signs of natural enemies or pathogens acting on FAW. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Gịnị ka m ga-eme ma m chọta egg mass ma ọ bụ obere larvae?
response: Ọ bụrụ na ọ ga-ekwe omume, tụgharịa ma mebie egg masses na obere larvae mgbe ị hụrụ ha. Nke a bụ otu n'ime usoro dị mfe n'ime integrated management nke FAO. Source: FAO, Integrated Management of FAW on Maize (2018).

instruction: Vision signal: 60% fall armyworm, 35% uncertain. Farmer: I see egg mass for leaf. Na FAW?
response: I no fit confirm from that alone. Is the egg mass covered with hairs or scales, and where exactly on the plant e dey? Source: CABI Fall Armyworm Field Handbook.

instruction: Àwọn ihò àtijọ́ wà, ṣùgbọ́n mi ò rí ìbàjẹ́ tuntun. Kí ni mo ṣe?
response: Má ṣe pinnu lórí àwọn ihò àtijọ́ nìkan. Ṣàyẹ̀wò ihò fún ìbàjẹ́ tuntun tàbí frass tuntun, kí o sì ka àwọn ewéko tó ní ìjàkadi lọ́wọ́ nìkan. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: I must see the caterpillar before I count the maize plant as infested?
response: No. FAO scouting method uses fresh damage or fresh frass in the whorl, so you fit count current infestation without finding the larva. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Farmer: I removed the caterpillars by hand.\nAssistant: Good; keep scouting.\nFarmer: They came back a week later. What should I do?
response: Resume weekly or more frequent scouting, inspect whorls for eggs and fresh feeding, and review whether natural enemies and other integrated practices are being conserved. Source: FAO, Integrated Management of FAW on Maize (2018).

instruction: Alamar hoton gona: 58% kwaron soja, 39% cutworm. Manomi: Ana yanke ƙananan masara. FAW ne?
response: Kada mu ɗauka haka nan. Shin ana yanke shukar kusa da saman ƙasa ne, ko kuma kuna ganin sabon cizo da bayan gari a cikin ramin? Source: FAO/CABI FAW identification guidance.

instruction: I see FAW eggs and small caterpillars. Wetin I fit do?
response: Where practical, remove and destroy egg masses and young larvae you find. Early manual action is part of FAO's integrated approach. Source: FAO, Integrated Management of FAW on Maize (2018).

instruction: Vision signal: 58% fall armyworm, 39% cutworm. Farmer: A na-ebipụ seedlings m. Ọ bụ FAW?
response: Ejila nke ahụ mee mkpebi ozugbo. A na-ebipụ seedling ahụ nso n'ala, ka ị na-ahụ mmebi ọhụrụ na frass n'olulu? Source: FAO/CABI FAW identification guidance.

instruction: Can planting maize late make FAW worse?
response: Late planting can expose young, tender maize to FAW pressure. FAO's Africa guidance recommends avoiding late planting as part of integrated management. Source: FAO, Five things to know about Fall Armyworm.

instruction: Vision signal: 58% fall armyworm, 39% cutworm. Farmer: The seedlings are being cut. Is it FAW?
response: Do not assume FAW. Is the damage at the soil line, or are there fresh holes and frass in the whorls? Also, can you find a larva during a careful inspection? Source: FAO/CABI FAW identification guidance.

instruction: Alamar hoton gona: 55% kwaron soja, 40% wata tsutsa. Manomi: Tsutsar ruwan kasa ce. Shin kwaron soja ne?
response: Kada mu yi zato daga launi kaɗai. Shin kan tsutsar yana da alamar Y mai juyewa, kuma akwai ɗigo huɗu masu duhu a sashen jiki kusa da ƙarshe? Source: CABI Fall Armyworm Field Handbook.

instruction: A yau barnar ta yi yawa, amma gobe ta yi kama da tsohuwa. Me zan yi?
response: Kada ka yanke shawara daga tsoffin ramuka kaɗai. Ka sake duba ramin don ganin sabuwar barna ko sabon bayan gari, sannan ka kirga shuke-shuken da ke fama a yanzu. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: What should I do after I find FAW in the field?
response: First confirm that the current damage and frass are consistent with FAW, record the affected area, and keep scouting. Use an integrated approach that combines monitoring, manual control, habitat/crop practices and conservation of natural enemies. Source: FAO, Integrated Management of FAW on Maize (2018).

instruction: Ṣé mo gbọ́dọ̀ rí ìdin náà kí n tó ka ewéko sí ẹni tí ọ̀gbìn ológun kọlu?
response: Rárá. Ọ̀nà FAO ń ka ewéko tó ní ìbàjẹ́ tuntun tàbí frass tuntun nínú ihò, bó tilẹ̀ jẹ́ pé a kò rí ìdin náà. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Can FAW live on crops other than maize?
response: Yes. FAW is polyphagous and can feed on many plant species, although maize is a preferred host. This is why scouting should consider the whole cropping system and not only a single plant. Source: FAO FAW Monitoring/Identification guidance.

instruction: Farmer: Enwere m ike iji insecticide ọzọ n'ihi na FAW alọghachila?\nAssistant: Chemical decision ga-esochi label nke product e debanyere aha.\nFarmer: Gịnị ka m ga-ele?
response: Lelee na product ahụ debanyere aha maka crop na pest dị na mpaghara gị, wee soro label maka ojiji, nchekwa na oge echere tupu owuwe ihe ubi. Ejila dose nke product ọzọ dochie ya. Source: FAO position on pesticide use for FAW.

instruction: Fall armyworm ga-ebelata mkpụrụ ọka m mgbe ọ bụla ọ mebiri akwụkwọ?
response: Ọ bụghị mgbe niile. Ọka nwere ike ịgbake site na mmebi akwụkwọ ụfọdụ, ya mere lelee infestation dị ugbu a kama iche na mmebi niile ga-eme ka mkpụrụ daa nke ukwuu. Source: FAO FAW management guidance (2018).

instruction: Are natural enemies useful against fall armyworm?
response: Yes. Ants, earwigs, pirate bugs, birds, parasitoid wasps and disease-causing organisms can attack FAW. Learn to recognize them and avoid unnecessary actions that destroy these natural enemies. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Shin duk barnar kwaron soja za ta rage yawan amfanin masara sosai?
response: Ba lallai ba ne. Masara na iya murmurewa daga wasu barnar ganye, don haka ka duba yawan shuke-shuken da ke da sabuwar barna maimakon ka ɗauka cewa duk barna za ta yi tsanani. Source: FAO FAW management guidance (2018).

instruction: Manomi: Barnar makon jiya tana nan.\nMataimaki: Ka kirga sabuwar barna kawai.\nManomi: Shin zan kirga tsohuwar shuka a yau?
response: A'a, ka kirga shuka ne idan akwai sabuwar barna ko sabon bayan gari da ke nuna cewa kwaron yana rayuwa a yanzu. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Manomi: Na ga ƙwai a kan ganye.\nMataimaki: Ka duba su sosai.\nManomi: Menene zan nema?
response: Nemi ko ƙwayayen suna cikin taro kuma suna da gashi ko sikeli a kansu; ka kuma duba ramin masara don sabon cizo. Idan ba ka da tabbaci, kar ka yi zato cewa FAW ne. Source: CABI Fall Armyworm Field Handbook.

instruction: Does finding adult moths prove that my maize is infested?
response: Adult moths show that FAW is present in or near the area, but they do not by themselves prove that a particular plant has a live larva. Inspect maize whorls for fresh damage or frass and record the findings. Source: FAO FAMEWS/FAW monitoring guidance.

instruction: Alamar hoton gona: 60% kwaron soja, 35% babu tabbas. Manomi: Na sami tarin ƙwai a kan ganyen masara. FAW ne?
response: Ba zan tabbatar daga wannan kaɗai ba. Shin tarin ƙwayayen yana da gashi ko sikeli a kansa, kuma a ina ne a shukar yake? Source: CABI Fall Armyworm Field Handbook.

instruction: How I go know say natural enemies dey attack FAW?
response: Look for dark or uneven egg masses, white silky parasitoid cocoons, and dead larvae that may be hard or soft. These can show natural enemies or pathogens are acting. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: What if the fall armyworm comes back after I remove the caterpillars?
response: Start systematic scouting again, look for fresh damage, frass, eggs and larvae, and check whether natural enemies and other integrated practices are being protected. Source: FAO, Integrated Management of FAW on Maize (2018).

instruction: Fall armyworm fit live for other crops apart from maize?
response: Yes. FAW can feed on many plant species, although maize is one of its preferred hosts. Source: FAO FAW Monitoring/Identification guidance.

instruction: Natural enemies fit help control fall armyworm?
response: Yes. Ants, earwigs, predatory bugs, birds, parasitoid wasps and some pathogens fit attack FAW. Learn to recognize them and protect them. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Farmer: Can I use another insecticide because FAW is back?\nAssistant: Chemical decisions must follow the locally registered product label.\nFarmer: What should I check before using one?
response: Check that the product is registered for the crop and pest in your area and follow its label for dose, protective measures and harvest interval. Do not assume a dose from another product or country is interchangeable. Source: FAO position on pesticide use for FAW.

instruction: Ṣé ọ̀gbìn ológun lè wà lórí irúgbìn mìíràn yàtọ̀ sí àgbàdo?
response: Bẹ́ẹ̀ni. FAW lè jẹ́ ọ̀pọ̀ irú ewéko, bó tilẹ̀ jẹ́ pé àgbàdo jẹ́ ọ̀kan lára àwọn ohun ọ̀gbìn tó fẹ́ràn jù. Nítorí náà, ṣàyẹ̀wò gbogbo eto oko. Source: FAO FAW Monitoring/Identification guidance.

instruction: Manomi: Zan iya amfani da wani maganin kwari saboda kwaron soja ya dawo?\nMataimaki: Dole ne a bi ka'idar samfurin da aka yi wa rajista.\nManomi: Me zan duba?
response: Ka tabbatar samfurin an yi masa rajista don amfanin gona da kwaron da ake sarrafawa a yankinka, sannan ka bi umarnin lakabi game da amfani da kariya da lokacin jira kafin girbi. Kada ka ɗauki adadin wani samfurin ka canza shi zuwa wani. Source: FAO position on pesticide use for FAW.

instruction: Intercropping fit help against fall armyworm?
response: Crop diversification fit reduce FAW pressure in some systems. A 2025 Nigeria study found lower FAW incidence and damage in maize intercropped with soybean than in sole maize. That result no be guarantee for every farm. Source: Jibril & Ahmed (2025), AGRIS.

instruction: Farmer: The field had FAW last week.\nAssistant: Record current infestation during scouting.\nFarmer: Is a damaged plant from last week counted today?
response: Only count a plant as currently infested when you see recent leaf damage or fresh frass indicating current activity. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: What is frass and why does it matter for FAW?
response: Frass is the sawdust-like insect waste found in or around the maize whorl. Fresh frass together with recent leaf damage indicates that a larva is currently feeding. Source: FAO Guidance Note 2 (2018); CABI Field Handbook.

instruction: Farmer: I find an egg mass on the maize leaf.\nAssistant: Check it closely.\nFarmer: Wetin I look for?
response: Look for an egg mass covered with hairs or scales and inspect the maize whorl for fresh damage. If you are not sure, do not guess; ask for more evidence. Source: CABI Fall Armyworm Field Handbook.

instruction: I find FAW for my maize. Wetin be the first thing to do?
response: First confirm fresh damage and fresh frass match FAW, record where the problem dey, and continue systematic scouting. Use several integrated methods and protect natural enemies. Source: FAO, Integrated Management of FAW on Maize (2018).

instruction: Kedu ihe na-egosi na natural enemies na-awakpo fall armyworm?
response: FAO kwuru na egg masses gbara ọchịchịrị ma ọ bụ na-adịghị nha, white silken cocoons nke parasitoids, na larvae nwụrụ anwụ nwere ike ịbụ ihe ịrịba ama nke natural enemies ma ọ bụ pathogens. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Farmer: Can I use another insecticide because FAW come back?\nAssistant: Chemical use must follow the registered product label.\nFarmer: Wetin I should check?
response: Confirm the product is registered for the crop and pest in your area, then follow its label for use, safety and harvest interval. No assume a dose from another product is the same. Source: FAO position on pesticide use for FAW.

instruction: Kedu ka m ga-esi nyochaa ubi m maka fall armyworm?
response: Gaa n'ubi n'ụdị W. N'isi, n'akụkụ ọ bụla nke ntụgharị, na njedebe, nyochaa osisi 10 n'ahịrị maka mmebi ọhụrụ ma ọ bụ frass ọhụrụ n'olulu, wee dekọọ osisi ndị nwere infestation ugbu a. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Adult FAW moth around my farm mean say every maize plant get the pest?
response: No. Adult moths show say FAW dey around, but you still need inspect maize whorls for fresh damage or frass to confirm current larval infestation. Source: FAO FAMEWS/FAW monitoring guidance.

instruction: Kí ni mo yẹ kí n kọ sílẹ̀ nígbà tí mo ń ṣàyẹ̀wò FAW?
response: Kọ plot tàbí oko, ọ̀nà tí o lò láti ṣàyẹ̀wò, iye ewéko tó ní ìjàkadi lọ́wọ́, ipò irúgbìn, àti àwọn ọ̀tá àdánidá tí o rí. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Ṣé gbogbo ìbàjẹ́ láti ọ̀dọ̀ ọ̀gbìn ológun máa dín ìkórè kù gidigidi?
response: Kì í ṣe bẹ́ẹ̀ ní gbogbo ìgbà. Àgbàdo lè bọ́ lára díẹ̀ nínú ìbàjẹ́ ewé, nítorí náà yẹ ìjàkadi tó ń ṣẹlẹ̀ lọ́wọ́ dípò kí o rò pé gbogbo ìbàjẹ́ yóò burú. Source: FAO FAW management guidance (2018).

instruction: Kí ni mo ṣe tí ọ̀gbìn ológun bá padà lẹ́yìn tí mo ti yọ ìdin?
response: Bẹ̀rẹ̀ ìwòran lẹ́ẹ̀kansi ní ọ̀nà tó ṣètò, wá ìbàjẹ́ tuntun, frass, ẹyin àti ìdin, kí o sì ṣàyẹ̀wò pé o ń dáàbò bo àwọn ọ̀tá àdánidá àti àwọn ìlànà mìíràn. Source: FAO, Integrated Management of FAW on Maize (2018).

instruction: Shin barnar ganye kaɗai ta isa in ce kwaron soja ne?
response: A'a. Ramukan sabbi da bayan gari a cikin ramin alamu ne masu ƙarfi, amma ka binciki tsutsar domin alamomin ganewa kafin ka tabbatar. Source: FAO Guidance Note 2 (2018); CABI Field Handbook.

instruction: Vision signal: 55% fall armyworm, 40% another caterpillar. Farmer: Caterpillar ahụ bụ brown. Ọ bụ FAW?
response: Ejila agba naanị mee mkpebi. Isi caterpillar nwere upside-down Y marking? E nwere ntụpọ ojii anọ n'akụkụ ahụ nke dị nso na ọdụ? Source: CABI Fall Armyworm Field Handbook.

instruction: Fall armyworm damage always mean say my maize yield go drop badly?
response: No be always. Maize fit compensate for some leaf damage, so scout current infestation and assess the field instead of assuming every damaged plant will lose most of its yield. Source: FAO FAW management guidance (2018).

instruction: Báwo ni mo ṣe yẹ kí n ṣàyẹ̀wò oko àgbàdo mi fún ọ̀gbìn ológun?
response: Fún oko kékeré, FAO dámọ̀ràn pé kí o wọ oko rẹ́ o kere tán lẹ́ẹ̀kan lọ́sẹ̀, kí o sì pọ̀ sí i nígbà tí ipò ń yí padà. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Kedu data m kwesịrị ide mgbe m na-scouting FAW?
response: Dee plot ma ọ bụ ubi, ụzọ i si nyochaa ya, ọnụ ọgụgụ osisi nwere infestation ugbu a, ọnọdụ crop, na natural enemies ị hụrụ. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Sai na ga tsutsar kwaron soja da ido kafin in kirga shukar?
response: A'a. Hanyar FAO tana kirga shuke-shuke da ke da sabuwar barna ko sabon bayan gari a cikin ramin, ko da ba ka ga tsutsar ba. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Sau nawa ya kamata in duba gonar masara don kwaron soja?
response: Ga karamar gona, FAO ta ba da shawarar shiga gona aƙalla sau ɗaya a mako, kuma a fi duba ta idan yanayi yana canzawa. Ka yi dubawa ta tsari, ba gefen gona kawai ba. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: I see old holes but no fresh frass. Wetin I suppose do?
response: No make treatment decision from old damage alone. Recheck the whorl for fresh damage or fresh frass and count only plants with current signs. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Vision signal: 51% fall armyworm, 46% stem borer. Farmer: My maize dey damage inside. Wetin I do?
response: I need one more clue before I identify am. The fresh damage dey inside the whorl with moist frass, or you see holes and dry sawdust-like material along the stalk? Source: FAO/CABI FAW identification guidance.

instruction: What should I do with FAW eggs and very young caterpillars?
response: When you find egg masses or young larvae on individual maize plants, remove and destroy them where practical. Early manual action is one of the low-risk options in FAO's integrated approach. Source: FAO, Integrated Management of FAW on Maize (2018).

instruction: Ọ ga-abụrịrị na m hụrụ caterpillar tupu m gụọ osisi dị ka ndị nwere fall armyworm?
response: Mba. Usoro FAO na-agụ osisi nwere mmebi akwụkwọ ọhụrụ ma ọ bụ frass ọhụrụ n'olulu, ọbụlagodi ma ọ bụrụ na a hụghị larva. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Ṣé ìbàjẹ́ ewé nìkan tó láti sọ pé ọ̀gbìn ológun ni?
response: Rárá. Àwọn ihò tuntun àti frass nínú ihò jẹ́ àmì tó lágbára, ṣùgbọ́n yẹ ìdin fún àwọn àmì ìdámọ̀ rẹ kí o tó dájú. Source: FAO Guidance Note 2 (2018); CABI Field Handbook.

instruction: My maize was damaged by FAW yesterday but looks better today. Should I keep treating?
response: Do not decide from old damage alone. Recheck the whorls for fresh damage or fresh frass and count only currently infested plants. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Farmer: Mmebi nke izu gara aga ka dị.\nAssistant: Gụọ mmebi ọhụrụ naanị.\nFarmer: Ya mere, m ga-agụ osisi ahụ taa?
response: Mba, gụọ ya dị ka current infestation naanị ma ọ bụrụ na e nwere mmebi ọhụrụ ma ọ bụ frass ọhụrụ nke na-egosi na pest ka nọ n'ebe ahụ. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: If my photo vision model says FAW is likely, should the assistant always agree?
response: No. When the vision score is close between FAW and another pest, the assistant should ask a targeted question about whorl damage, fresh frass or diagnostic larval markings before naming the pest. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018); CABI Field Handbook.

instruction: Mo ti rí ọ̀gbìn ológun nínú oko. Kí ni ìgbésẹ̀ àkọ́kọ́?
response: Kọ́kọ́ jẹ́risi pé ìbàjẹ́ tuntun àti frass tuntun bá ọ̀gbìn ológun mu, kọ ibi tó kan sílẹ̀, kí o sì tẹ̀síwájú pẹ̀lú ìwòran. Lo àwọn ọ̀nà púpọ̀ papọ̀, pẹ̀lú ìṣàkóso àti dídáàbò bo àwọn ọ̀tá àdánidá. Source: FAO, Integrated Management of FAW on Maize (2018).

instruction: Why is FAW difficult to see during the day?
response: Larvae often remain hidden in the maize whorl, so looking only at the leaf surface can miss them. Fresh whorl damage and frass can reveal active feeding even when the larva is not visible. Source: CABI Fall Armyworm Field Handbook; FAO Guidance Note 2.

instruction: Vision signal: 55% fall armyworm, 40% another caterpillar. Farmer: The caterpillar brown. Na FAW?
response: No guess from colour alone. Does the caterpillar have the pale upside-down Y on its head, and four dark spots near the last body segment? Source: CABI Fall Armyworm Field Handbook.

instruction: Farmer: I found armyworm damage yesterday.\nAssistant: Check the whorls for fresh damage and frass.\nFarmer: Most holes are old and there is no fresh frass. Should I spray?
response: Do not treat based on old damage alone. Resample the field and count only plants with current signs of infestation. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Yaya zan yi samfurin binciken kwaron soja a gonar?
response: Yi tafiya mai siffar W a gonar. A farko, a kowane juyi, da ƙarshe, duba shuke-shuke 10 a jere don sabon lalacewa ko sabon bayan gari a cikin ramin, sannan ka rubuta adadin shuke-shuken da ke fama a yanzu. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Shin ƙwari masu amfani suna taimakawa wajen sarrafa kwaron soja?
response: Eh. Tururuwa, earwig, kwari masu farauta, tsuntsaye, parasitoid wasps da wasu ƙwayoyin cuta na halitta suna iya kai wa kwaron soja hari. Ka koyi gane su kuma ka kare su. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Shin haɗa masara da wani amfanin gona na iya taimakawa?
response: Haɗa amfanin gona na iya rage matsin kwaron soja a wasu tsarin noma. Wani bincike na Najeriya na 2025 ya sami ƙarancin barnar FAW a masarar da aka haɗa da waken soya fiye da masara ita kaɗai. Wannan sakamakon ba garanti ba ne ga kowace gona. Source: Jibril & Ahmed (2025), AGRIS.

instruction: Àgbẹ̀: Ìbàjẹ́ ọ̀sẹ̀ tó kọjá ṣi wà.\nOlùrànlọ́wọ́: Ka ìbàjẹ́ tuntun nìkan.\nÀgbẹ̀: Ṣé mo ka ewéko yẹn lónìí?
response: Rárá. Kà á gẹ́gẹ́ bí ìjàkadi tó ń ṣẹlẹ̀ lọ́wọ́ nìkan tí o bá rí ìbàjẹ́ tuntun tàbí frass tuntun tó ń fi hàn pé kokoro náà ṣì wà. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Do I have to find the caterpillar during scouting?
response: No. FAO's scouting method counts plants with recent leaf damage or fresh frass in the whorl, so the method can be fast and non-destructive without finding the larva itself. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: What should I record while scouting FAW?
response: Record the field or plot, sampling route, number of currently infested plants, crop condition and observations of natural enemies. Consistent records help you compare changes over time. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Ṣé àwọn ọ̀tá àdánidá ń rànwọ́ lórí ọ̀gbìn ológun?
response: Bẹ́ẹ̀ni. Àwọn èèrà, earwig, àwọn kòkòrò tó ń dọdẹ, ẹyẹ, parasitoid wasps àti àwọn àrùn kan lè pa ọ̀gbìn ológun. Kọ́ ẹ̀kọ́ láti mọ̀ wọ́n, kí o sì dáàbò bò wọ́n. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).
